Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-09-01", "authors": [{"authorId": "2186278677", "name": "Chen Lin"}, {"authorId": "2152513104", "name": "Lei Wang"}, {"authorId": "2108505046", "name": "Yin Zhang"}, {"authorId": "2279996835", "name": "Wei Liu"}, {"authorId": "2354507778", "name": "Ye Luo"}, {"authorId": "2155452053", "name": "Qing-Qiang Wu"}], "abstract": "Capturing global context through attention is essential for reasoning over knowledge graphs, especially when relevant entities are distant or disconnected. To scale attention to large graphs, recent methods replace Softmax with kernel feature mappings, reducing computational complexity to linear in the number of nodes. While efficient, these approximations tend to produce overly smooth attention scores, which can reduce discrimination between correct triplets and hard negative samples. Moreover, they exhibit scale-dependent shifts in attention entropy, making them sensitive to changes in graph size during inductive inference. In this paper, we introduce LaGR, a novel approach for integrating global information in knowledge graph reasoning. Rather than approximating interactions among all nodes, LaGR compresses the graph into a fixed, compact set of latent summaries and applies exact self-attention within this latent space. This change yields scale-invariant attention and stable performance across diverse data settings. In addition, we propose a node-adaptive residual fusion mechanism that dynamically balances local and global information at the node level, leading to more expressive representations. Extensive experiments on both transductive and inductive benchmarks show that LaGR substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, demonstrating that exact attention over latent summaries is an efficient and effective way to capture global context in knowledge graph reasoning. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/XMU-KG/LaGR."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "1f5509395a41ed509ada87bd3f75be0b370fe546", "externalIds": {"DOI": "10.1016/j.knosys.2026.117091", "CorpusId": 292244022}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/1f5509395a41ed509ada87bd3f75be0b370fe546", "title": "RMKGC: Rationale-Guided Reasoning with LLM for Multimodal Knowledge Graph Completion", "venue": "Knowledge-Based Systems", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": "CLOSED", "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1016/j.knosys.2026.117091?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.1016/j.knosys.2026.117091, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-01-23", "authors": [{"authorId": "2336081900", "name": "Yan Feng"}, {"authorId": "2293945751", "name": "Haitao Yu"}], "abstract": "Existing knowledge graph completion models based on convolutional neural networks still face limitations in feature representation. The unified convolutional perspective struggles to fully capture local variations within complex structures. And when feature dimensions increase significantly, redundant information may obscure key features. To address these issues, this paper proposes a knowledge graph completion model based on multi-channel dynamic convolutional network. The model first employs a reshaping combined with a dynamic convolution kernel mechanism to achieve local adaptive modeling and deep latent feature extraction. Subsequently, it introduces alternating reshaping and static convolution kernel structures to extract multi-scale surface features, thereby balancing feature diversity and global consistency. Finally, a self-calibrating attention mechanism selects the most representative features. Experiments on four public benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed model achieves significant performance improvements over existing methods in link prediction tasks, validating its effectiveness in modeling complex relationships and feature representation."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "7d7b14f8e7ff281f38bc977122a6e367ba8eae76", "externalIds": {"DBLP": "journals/comintsys/LiuWCS26", "DOI": "10.1007/s40747-025-02225-9", "CorpusId": 284891447}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/7d7b14f8e7ff281f38bc977122a6e367ba8eae76", "title": "TPSformer: knowledge graph representation learning with text and position structure for link prediction", "venue": "Complex & Intelligent Systems", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 2, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "https://doi.org/10.1007/s40747-025-02225-9", "status": "GOLD", "license": "CCBYNCND", "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1007/s40747-025-02225-9?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.1007/s40747-025-02225-9, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-01-19", "authors": [{"authorId": "2395524700", "name": "Yi Liu"}, {"authorId": "2260710028", "name": "Qing-Wang Wang"}, {"authorId": "2380147592", "name": "Wei Chen"}, {"authorId": "2260711072", "name": "Tao Shen"}], "abstract": "Transformers, leveraging the powerful self-attention (SA) mechanism, effectively model long-range dependencies and complex relationships between elements, demonstrating outstanding performance in natural language tasks. However, when processing knowledge graph (KG) triples, they still face two major challenges: First, their vector representations often struggle to fully capture the fine-grained text semantic information inherent within triples. Second, the SA mechanism lacks explicit differentiation between the distinct roles of head, relation, and tail nodes within triples. In particular, due to structural limitations, the vanilla transformer struggles to model latent semantic and structural information directly between nodes. To address this, this paper proposes a transformer model that integrates text information with Positional Structure (TPSformer). This approach leverages the Pre-trained Language Model (PLM) to extract node text features, thereby better utilizing text semantic information within KG. Subsequently, we design a position-aware encoder that integrates textual features to enhance the SA mechanism\u2019s modeling capability for relational semantics, enabling node representations to simultaneously incorporate textual and positional structural information. Experimental results on three real-world KG link prediction datasets demonstrate that by integrating text semantics and explicitly distinguishing the positional roles of nodes within triples, our method more effectively captures complex semantic relationships between entities and relations. Our approach significantly improves link prediction performance, outperforming current state-of-the-art models."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "f53fb9a4149ff78e11877c1aa9156104b112ea9e", "externalIds": {"DBLP": "journals/asc/LeeL26", "DOI": "10.1016/j.asoc.2026.114627", "CorpusId": 284617054}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/f53fb9a4149ff78e11877c1aa9156104b112ea9e", "title": "FT-MixE: Fourier transform-based efficient mixing of knowledge graph embeddings for improved link prediction", "venue": "Applied Soft Computing", "year": 2026, "citationCount": 1, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asoc.2026.114627", "status": "HYBRID", "license": "CCBYNCND", "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1016/j.asoc.2026.114627?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asoc.2026.114627, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2026-01-01", "authors": [{"authorId": "2163906186", "name": "MyoungHoon Lee"}, {"authorId": "2356003874", "name": "Junghye Lee"}], "abstract": null}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "6f5f8fdada458038cae8196db0d7fa1ae9d76d51", "externalIds": {"PubMedCentral": "12830770", "DOI": "10.1038/s41598-025-32952-5", "CorpusId": 284056626, "PubMed": "41422306"}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/6f5f8fdada458038cae8196db0d7fa1ae9d76d51", "title": "Graph transformer for link prediction on N-ary facts", "venue": "Scientific Reports", "year": 2025, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-32952-5_reference.pdf", "status": "GOLD", "license": "CCBYNCND", "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12830770, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2025-12-20", "authors": [{"authorId": "2223848225", "name": "Bin Hu"}, {"authorId": "2213470960", "name": "Xiongjie Tao"}, {"authorId": "2200815108", "name": "Hui Guo"}, {"authorId": "91028496", "name": "Jie-Cheng Li"}, {"authorId": "2313797696", "name": "Guangyao Pang"}, {"authorId": "2363674780", "name": "Diana Xie"}], "abstract": "Hyper-relational knowledge graphs build upon traditional knowledge graphs to enhance the diversity and complexity of information representation. They achieve this by integrating multi-dimensional auxiliary information with standard triples. However, this characteristic introduces certain challenges to the task of N-ary Fact Link Prediction. Unlike binary relational knowledge representations, N-ary Facts have more complex and varied expression forms. To address the issue of insufficient utilization of heterogeneous graph structure information in existing N-ary Fact representation methods, this paper proposes an N-ary graph Transformer model. This model incorporates a new attention mechanism based on N-ary structural bias. By improving the representation of N-ary heterogeneous graphs, it more accurately identifies key associations in recommendation scenarios. Experimental validations on the JF17K, Wikipeople, and WD50K datasets demonstrate that the NAGT model outperforms comparative methods in extracting structural information. It effectively completes the knowledge graph and shows both efficiency and robustness in experiments related to the N-ary Fact Link Prediction task."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "c86b3c6e5c0df8da6d49fb40e3ef8f98b509ef36", "externalIds": {"DBLP": "conf/bigdataconf/LiuPYC25", "DOI": "10.1109/BigData66926.2025.11402131", "CorpusId": 286328669}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/c86b3c6e5c0df8da6d49fb40e3ef8f98b509ef36", "title": "Multi-Feature Fusion Strategies for Enhancing Knowledge Graph Embedding", "venue": "BigData Congress [Services Society]", "year": 2025, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": "CLOSED", "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1109/BigData66926.2025.11402131?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.1109/BigData66926.2025.11402131, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2025-12-08", "authors": [{"authorId": "2422547071", "name": "Chenchen Liu"}, {"authorId": "3040861", "name": "Fei Pu"}, {"authorId": "2257377068", "name": "Bai-Lin Yang"}, {"authorId": "2375130510", "name": "Lirong Cheng"}], "abstract": "Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE) is essential for representing entities and relations in large-scale knowledge graphs, yet existing neural approaches struggle with modeling complex relational patterns and integrating heterogeneous features. We propose a novel Multi-Feature Fusion Embedding (MFFE) framework that addresses these challenges through four specialized modules: the Relation-Conditioned Neighborhood Aggregator (RCNA), the Dynamic Relation Modulator (DRM), the Entity-Relation Attention Module (ERAM), and the Adaptive Feature Fusion Module (AFFM). These modules enable finegrained feature extraction and adaptive fusion by integrating neighborhood, relation-aware, and interaction features through deep neural networks, yielding robust and expressive entity and relation embeddings. Extensive experiments on five benchmark knowledge graph datasets, FB15k-237, YAGO3-10, WN18RR, KINSHIP, and UMLS, demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models, achieving superior performance on link prediction tasks."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "8eb00d82b428a30ec4bf4736ecf97a352510272d", "externalIds": {"DBLP": "journals/tnn/HaoHBJGSY26", "DOI": "10.1109/TNNLS.2025.3618611", "CorpusId": 282810238, "PubMed": "41191464"}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/8eb00d82b428a30ec4bf4736ecf97a352510272d", "title": "Multimodal Knowledge Graph Completion by Cross-Modal Interaction With Similarity Enhancing and Difference Embracing", "venue": "IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems", "year": 2025, "citationCount": 2, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1109/TNNLS.2025.3618611?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.1109/TNNLS.2025.3618611, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2025-11-05", "authors": [{"authorId": "2386091867", "name": "Linjia Hao"}, {"authorId": "2140879677", "name": "Yong-Li Hu"}, {"authorId": "2467523752", "name": "Bie Tong"}, {"authorId": "3371529", "name": "Huajie Jiang"}, {"authorId": "2261897593", "name": "Jun-Bin Gao"}, {"authorId": "5305357", "name": "Yan-Feng Sun"}, {"authorId": "2239088112", "name": "Bao-Cai Yin"}], "abstract": "Multimodal knowledge graph completion (MMKGC) enhances the precision and breadth of application of knowledge graphs by integrating rich data from various modalities, steadily increasing its appeal in the research community. Prior studies mainly focus on the common representation of different modalities while neglecting the different and complementary features. On the contrary, some works tend to model triples of each modality separately while overlooking the similarities between modalities. It is challenging to associate the heterogeneous modalities effectively for MMKGC. In this article, we introduce a novel MMKGC framework by cross-modal interaction with similarity-enhancing and difference-embracing (CISEDE), which leverages both the similarities and differences among multimodal entities by a proposed cross-modal interaction mechanism. In the cross-modal interaction, multihead attention is employed to enhance similarity information from multimodal entities and embrace different information by linking various modal triples. Through relation-guided fusion, the modal triples are decoded and merged for MMKGC. The experimental results on three commonly used datasets, FB15k-237, WN9, and WN18RR, show that the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "5793d4cf3595610dad58bf8093340a7ce7d9ca76", "externalIds": {"DOI": "10.3390/electronics14204127", "CorpusId": 282283276}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/5793d4cf3595610dad58bf8093340a7ce7d9ca76", "title": "Multi-Chain Fusion Reasoning for Knowledge Graph Link Prediction", "venue": "Electronics", "year": 2025, "citationCount": 1, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/20/4127/pdf?version=1761053159", "status": "GOLD", "license": "CCBY", "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.3390/electronics14204127?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics14204127, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2025-10-21", "authors": [{"authorId": "2122805421", "name": "Shao-Nian Huang"}, {"authorId": "2382887509", "name": "Peilin Li"}, {"authorId": "2382816507", "name": "Huanran Wang"}, {"authorId": "2382732383", "name": "Zhixin Chen"}], "abstract": "The knowledge graph link prediction task currently faces challenges such as insufficient semantic fusion of structured knowledge and unstructured text, limited representation learning of long-tailed entities, and insufficient interpretability of the reasoning process. Aiming at the above problems, this paper proposes a multi-chain fusion reasoning framework to realize accurate link prediction. First, a dual retrieval mechanism based on semantic similarity metrics and embedded feature matching is designed to construct a high-confidence candidate entity set; second, entity-attribute chains, entity-relationship chains, and historical context chains are established by integrating context information from external knowledge bases to generate a candidate entity set. Finally, a self-consistency scoring method fusing type constraints and semantic space alignment is proposed to realize the joint validation of structural rationality and semantic relevance of candidate entities. Experiments on two public datasets show that the method in this paper fully utilizes the ability of multi-chain reasoning and significantly improves the accuracy of knowledge graph link prediction."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "4bac0ebc27b327a5e78202ae065f8ad42de15f57", "externalIds": {"DBLP": "journals/concurrency/LinRLRZC25", "DOI": "10.1002/cpe.70253", "CorpusId": 282232063}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/4bac0ebc27b327a5e78202ae065f8ad42de15f57", "title": "A Nested Dual Encoder\u2010Decoder Representation Model Based on Entity\u2010Relation Interaction Effects for Knowledge Graph Link Prediction", "venue": "Concurrency and Computation", "year": 2025, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1002/cpe.70253?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.1002/cpe.70253, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2025-10-16", "authors": [{"authorId": "2293763352", "name": "Jiarun Lin"}, {"authorId": "47936498", "name": "Xiao-Li Ren"}, {"authorId": "2315139109", "name": "Xiao-Yong Li"}, {"authorId": "1787563", "name": "Kai-Jun Ren"}, {"authorId": "2293655352", "name": "Xiang Zhu"}, {"authorId": "2346545400", "name": "Xinyu Chen"}], "abstract": "Knowledge graph embedding (KGE) offers a more intuitive approach to discovering potential relations between known entities. However, current models are associated with challenges such as a large number of training parameters and low training efficiency and fail to provide in\u2010depth analysis of the impact of embedding dimensionality on entities and relations in link prediction performance. Therefore, we investigate the impact of entity and relation embedding dimensions on their interaction and assess how these dimensions affect the performance of KGE models. Based on these insights, we propose a novel dual encoder\u2010decoder model, NDcRE, which includes decoders MlpD and AttnMlpD, designed to capture long\u2010distance interactions and improve link prediction performance with fewer parameters. Evaluated on four benchmarks, WN18RR, FB15k\u2010237, DB100k, and YAGO3\u201010, NDcRE significantly improves model efficiency by utilizing fewer parameters and dimensions, thereby enhancing both its utility and convenience. In particular, the AttnMlpD decoder further reduces the model's training parameters, enabling it to deliver strong performance even in environments with limited computational resources."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "7beb359af090255f040aad8d31932f17677b30bf", "externalIds": {"DOI": "10.1109/CAC67268.2025.11487445", "CorpusId": 287965389}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/7beb359af090255f040aad8d31932f17677b30bf", "title": "A Graph Structure-Enhanced GNN Encoder with Semantic Matching Decoder for KG Completion", "venue": "ACM Cloud and Autonomic Computing Conference", "year": 2025, "citationCount": 0, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": "CLOSED", "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: The following paper fields have been elided by the publisher: {'abstract'}. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use."}, "publicationDate": "2025-08-22", "authors": [{"authorId": "2352828454", "name": "Jinlan Kong"}, {"authorId": "2283076654", "name": "Xiao-Hui He"}, {"authorId": "2378105536", "name": "Haichuan Fang"}, {"authorId": "2376791738", "name": "Roujia Ji"}, {"authorId": "2329857104", "name": "Pengcheng Yang"}, {"authorId": "2407886998", "name": "Shuang Li"}, {"authorId": "2353793472", "name": "Haofei Li"}, {"authorId": "2353066690", "name": "Haonan Sun"}, {"authorId": "51432923", "name": "Meng-Jia Qiao"}, {"authorId": "153091903", "name": "Panle Li"}, {"authorId": "153033126", "name": "Xijie Cheng"}, {"authorId": "2377544903", "name": "Qinglei Zhou"}, {"authorId": "2352904195", "name": "Jiandong Shang"}], "abstract": "Geographic knowledge graphs (GeoKGs) describe and simulate geographic phenomena by storing geographic entities with their semantic relations, providing a foundation for many real-world tasks such as urban function identification. However, GeoKGs are often incomplete due to manual construction, leading to inaccurate and/or suboptimal decision-making. This situation requires GeoKG inference (GeoKGI), which involves learning new knowledge by projecting entities and relations into embedding spaces to infer missing facts and complete GeoKGs. Nevertheless, current inference methods mainly focus on modeling universal knowledge graphs (KGs), which cannot be directly transferred into GeoKGs as, unlike KGs, their entities contain specific class information. Inference methods on universal KGs lack a clear manner of modeling such entity class information. Moreover, they often ignore the representation learning of relations, resulting in inadequate modeling of GeoKGs.
